topic: How does the 45° scan range affect link budget calculations for edge-of-coverage users compared to broadside beams?
consensus_response: A 45° scan range leads to increased first side lobes (SLLs), reducing effective radiated power and link budget. This is due to the off-focus illumination of beamformers, causing SLLs to increase with scan angle. For v-polarized outermost beams, SLLs reach -11 dB at 30 GHz. The quasi-TEM mode's frequency dispersion exacerbates this effect, leading to faster increases in SLLs with scan angle. Consequently, link budget calculations must account for these variations to ensure reliable data transmission for edge-of-coverage users.
reference_context: The reference context provides information on the impact of 45° scan range on antenna performance, including increased first side lobes (SLLs) and beam squint due to frequency dispersion. The quasi-TEM mode's effect is more pronounced in v-polarized beams, leading to reduced effective radiated power and link budget.
